To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cytostatic drug methylglyoxal‐bis(guanylhydrazine), which interferes with the polyamine metabolism and function, is rapidly taken up by leukemia cells and is retained in these cells for several days, and that the intracellular concentrations of methylglyoxyl‐bis(guanylhrazine) in the leukemia cells can be determined by simple chemical assays.

the drug methylglyoxal (MG) bis(guanyl)hydrazone (BG) is a potent inhibitor of polyamine biosynthesis, that it is rapidly taken up by cells, that its uptake is critically dependent on the proliferation rate of the cells, that it is retained in the circulation of leukemic patients for several days, and that it is an effective antitumor agent in man.
methylglyoxalg bis(guanyl­hydrazone) is rapidly taken up by leukemia cells, resulting in the formation within the cells of a concentration gradient that is distinctly anti‐prolifera­tive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a rational basis for the use of methylglyoxa1 bis(guanyl‐hydrazone) as a chemotherapeutic agent in human cancer, with special emphasis on leukemia and lymphoma.
the development of a new approach to cancer chemotherapy based on the use of methylglyoxyl bis(guanyl hydrazone), a drug which is selectively toxic for proliferating cells.
the development of new antineoplastic drugs which are selectively cytotoxic to rapidly dividing cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

methylglyoxalg bis‐(guanyhydrazone) is an effective drug for the treatment of human leukemia, the drug being rapidly taken up into the leukemia cells, and the concentrations of drug in the cells being maintained for a period of days.
the drug is taken up rapidly and retained in leukemia cells for a long time and that the drug concentrations in leukemia cells can be monitored by the assay described here.

methylglyoxalg bis(guanyl‐hydrazone), in contrast to many other cytostatic compounds, is not only rapidly taken up by leukemia cells but is also retained by the cells for prolonged periods of time, thus allowing a relatively long‐term exposure of the leukemia cells to the cytostatic drug.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
methylglyoxalg bis(guanyl‐ hydrazone) is a highly potent cytotoxic compound which, however, is only effective at concentrations which are difficult to attain and maintain in the blood plasma.
the cytotoxic action of methylglyox al bis(guanyl hydrazone) is critically dependent on the drug's concentration in the target cells.
methylglyoxol bis(guanyl hydrazone) has been found to be a highly effective antitumor drug in vitro and in vivo in the treatment of human leukemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
methylglyoxalone bis(guanyl hydrazone) is a promising new antineoplastic agent, and that its clinical usefulness may be improved by regular assays of cellular drug concentrations.
